key_insight: ToM2Vec uses continuous latent tokens to represent possible partner states, improving multi-agent coordination beyond text-based theory-of-mind reasoning.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a compact mechanism for conditioning agents’ decisions on inferred partner beliefs and intentions, including when interacting with unseen partner model families.
method: Learn a fixed budget of continuous theory-of-mind tokens in latent space.
Supervise tokens during training using the partner’s actual thoughts.
Generate tokens at test time to condition each agent’s thoughts and actions.
evidence_signal: Across five environments spanning collaborative, competitive, and mixed-motive interactions, the abstract reports consistent gains over base and baseline models, weaker performance with text reasoning, and transfer to unseen partner models.
watch_item: Training requires access to partner thoughts for supervision; the abstract does not quantify performance gains or computational overhead.
paper_title: ToM2Vec: Continuous Theory-of-Mind Tokens for Multi-Agent Coordination
